title: Canonical ordinary tensor germ coordinates
statement: For the commuting restricted pullback square of [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition] and a complex P, four compatible stalk ring equivalences, an eA-semilinear input chain iso alpha, and a tensor chain iso tau exist. Tau sends c tensor q to eC(c) tensor alpha(q). Moreover, in every degree, tau followed by the ambient tensorStalkIso equals the restricted tensorStalkIso followed by stalks of [def-pc-open-pinned-single-tensor-restriction-iso] inverse and the additive same-germ comparison obtained from overFunctorEquiv and restrictStalkNatIso. No derived homology equation is asserted.

source.place: sheaves.tex, lemma-stalk-pullback-modules (Tag 0098); perfect.tex, equation-bc (Tag 0DJ7), ordinary target path; cohomology.tex, exact localization Tags 08HY and 08DW.

proof.text: Use the proved inverse open inclusion ring coordinates, endpoint transport and stalk-map composition identities to obtain all four ring compatibilities and canonical normalization of the input and output ring equivalences.

Use the proved canonical semilinear input-complex isomorphism. Its component formula identifies the input coordinate with the overFunctorEquiv/restrictStalkNatIso map followed by point transport from hj. Rewrite its scalar equivalence using the input ring normalization.
Apply the proved generic semilinear tensor-complex transport using the A-to-C compatibility. This constructs the tensor chain isomorphism and its pure-tensor formula.

Use the pinned comparison generator equation with the normalized output ring map. Substitute the canonical input component formula, then extend the equation from pure tensors to arbitrary tensors by TensorProduct.induction_on, using additivity for the zero and sum cases.
